Works today because new records were never persisted, but the two removal paths (cancel vs delete) look interchangeable and the next change (e.g. auto-creating hosts) will make cancel silently drop server-side work; also delete passes this.get('host') to deleteHost after destroy resolves, relying on the record still being in the array.

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host` the `cancel()` branch that calls `sendAction('deleteHost', host)` only runs when `host.isNew` is true (i.e., a record created client-side via `store.createRecord('embeddable-host')` and not yet saved). In that case, not calling `destroyRecord` is consistent: there is nothing persisted on the server to delete. The actual delete path (`delete()` action) is only exposed in the non-editing UI (i.e., for existing records) and correctly calls `destroyRecord()` before removing from the array. The finding’s concerns about “interchangeable semantics” and “next change (auto-creating hosts)” are speculative and not a verifiable defect from this diff; additionally, passing the same record object to `deleteHost` after `destroyRecord` resolves is sufficient for `removeObject` to work.
